headlines.title: GE Q3 Deep Dive: Market Reacts to Margin Pressure Despite Strong Service Demand
headlines.summary: Industrial conglomerate GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 17.5% year on year to $13.29 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.25 per share was 12% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

headlines.title: GE Stock Rises Premarket: GE Aerospace CEO Assures Demand Remains 'Solid,' Retail Agrees
headlines.summary: CEO Larry Culp cited solid demand as third-quarter revenue rose 18% and profit jumped 30%.

headlines.title: General Electric (GE) Stock Drops As Q3 Results Spotlight Margin Strength
headlines.summary: General Electric just reported Q3 2026 results that put profit quality at the center of the story, yet the stock fell 3.7% to US$299.87 by the close. Earnings per share landed a little above US$2.30 and operating margin in GE Aerospace reached the low 20s, pointing to profit resilience even as sentiment cooled. This is a margin season for GE.

headlines.title: The Big Concern Behind GE’s Earnings Beat Stock Tumble
headlines.summary: The company reported third-quarter earnings per share of $2.25 from sales of $13.3 billion. Wall Street was looking for earnings per share of $2.01 on sales of $12.9 billion.

headlines.title: GE Aerospace Posts Record Q3 Results: Time to Buy the Dip?
headlines.summary: GE Aerospace's record Q3 results and raised guidance highlight strong commercial engine demand, but does the stock's recent pullback and premium valuation present a buying opportunity?

description: General Electric Company, doing business as GE Aerospace, designs and produces commercial and defense aircraft engines, integrated engine components, electric power, and aircraft systems. The company operates through two segments, Commercial Engines & Services, and Defense & Propulsion Technologies. The Commercial Engines & Services segment designs, develops, manufactures, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services of jet engines and sale of spare parts for commercial airframes, business aviation, and aeroderivative applications. The Defense & Propulsion Technologies designs, develops, manufactures, and services jet engines and avionics and power systems for governments, militaries, and commercial airframers, as well as MRO of engines and the sale of spare parts. This segment also offers aircraft components and systems, such as small turboprop engines, aeroengine mechanical transmissions, turbines, combustors and controls, additive manufacturing, propeller systems, ignition systems, sensors and engine accessories for fixed wing and rotorcraft applications for commercial and military end users under the Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers, and Colibrium Additive brands. The company operates in the United States, Europe, Asia, the Americas, the Middle East, and Africa. General Electric Company was incorporated in 1892 and is based in Evendale, Ohio.
